definition: The central axiom of the WLU authority: WLU represents a dimensionless normalized amount of work, decoupled from financial currency or chargeback rates.
The second axis of workload demand, representing the required delivery rate to perform work at a requested pace.
Budget constraints where a single reservation is checked against the leaf and every ancestor; the same spend is reflected at each level and is not summed across them.
The phase where actual performed work is recorded as spent WLU and any unused work ceiling or delivery capacity is released.
A business obligation consisting of a budget and a fallback graph of implementation stages.
An authenticated planning intent for a rescue stage that reserves zero account or hierarchy WLU and zero delivery capacity.
A failure indicating insufficient admitted work entitlement; a budget problem, not a capacity problem.
A failure indicating temporary token/burst capacity is unavailable; typically accompanied by a retry-after value.
A failure indicating the requested WLU/s delivery rate cannot currently be reserved.
